name: 331. OpenAI image generation and edit: undeliverable fields refused, moderation blocks classified, image count reported, link inputs sent as links (openai image fields) [SERIAL]
description: TXE-6528 regression, contract C3, C4, C5, C6. Local fixture regression, no live provider calls: run with providerErrorFixture=1 against the gateway of tests/e2e/api/provider_config/provider-error-fixture.config.json, with tests/e2e/api/runners/provider-error-fixture.mjs as the only upstream. The openai provider's base URL is the fixture, which answers /v1/images/generations and /v1/images/edits in the gpt-image shape (n images, OpenAI's token usage, no image count) and answers model gpt-image-blocked with OpenAI's documented moderation block (HTTP 400, code moderation_blocked). Every row names the key with x-bf-api-key and reads back from /__wire the requests that reached the fixture. Pinned: a generation request carrying aspect_ratio, input_images, type or resolution, which OpenAI's images API has no field for, is answered 400 caller_unsupported_parameter with error.param naming the field and makes no upstream call (before, the field was sent under a name OpenAI does not know, or dropped); a moderation block keeps OpenAI's 400 and code and carries error_type caller_content_filtered, from one upstream call, on generation and edit; a two-image response carries usage.output_images 2 next to the token usage; an edit whose input images are links reaches OpenAI as its JSON edit body with images[].image_url equal to the links (before, each link was written as an empty multipart file part), and an edit with an uploaded file is still a multipart form; a streamed edit with link inputs (stream true, JSON or multipart at the client) reaches OpenAI as the same JSON body with stream set, and the partial and completed events come back with the token usage. The azure provider's endpoint is the same fixture (its images path is /openai/v1/images/generations): the refusal holds on azure through /v1/images/generations and through the Azure deployments drop-in route, and an azure request with deliverable fields makes its one call. The link host images.example.invalid does not resolve, so a gateway that tried to download an input image would fail the row. Whether OpenAI charges for a moderation-blocked image is not documented and is not pinned here. Run the whole folder in order.

item.name: [EXPECT-400] openai/gpt-image-1.5 /v1/images/generations with aspect_ratio is refused naming the field, before any upstream call (openai image fields)

exec: if (pm.variables.get('providerErrorFixture') !== '1') {
pm.execution.skipRequest();
pm.sendRequest({ url: pm.variables.get('providerErrorFixtureUrl') + '/__reset', method: 'POST' }, function (err, res) {
pm.test('openai image fields setup: the fixture was reset', function () {
pm.expect(err, String(err)).to.equal(null);
pm.expect(res.code).to.equal(200);
var FX = pm.variables.get('providerErrorFixtureUrl');
// wire: the requests that reached the fixture, bytes as they arrived.

function wire(cb) { pm.sendRequest({ url: FX + '/__wire', method: 'GET' }, function (err, res) { pm.test('the fixture answered /__wire', function () { pm.expect(err, String(err)).to.equal(null); pm.expect(res.code).to.equal(200); }); cb(res.json().data[0].calls); }); }
function imageCalls(calls) { return calls.filter(function (c) { return c.path === '/v1/images/generations' || c.path === '/v1/images/edits'; }); }
pm.test('the client gets 400', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.equal(400); });
var body = pm.response.json();
pm.test('error_type is caller_unsupported_parameter', function () { pm.expect(body.extra_fields && body.extra_fields.error_type, pm.response.text()).to.equal('caller_unsupported_parameter'); });
pm.test('error.param names the field', function () { pm.expect(body.error && body.error.param, pm.response.text()).to.equal('aspect_ratio'); });
wire(function (calls) { pm.test('no upstream call was made', function () { pm.expect(imageCalls(calls), JSON.stringify(calls)).to.have.length(0); }); });

item.name: openai/gpt-image-1.5 /v1/images/edits JSON stream with images given as links: the JSON edit body carries stream and the link unchanged, and the events come back (openai image fields)

exec: if (pm.variables.get('providerErrorFixture') !== '1') {
pm.execution.skipRequest();
pm.sendRequest({ url: pm.variables.get('providerErrorFixtureUrl') + '/__reset', method: 'POST' }, function (err, res) {
pm.test('openai image fields setup: the fixture was reset', function () {
pm.expect(err, String(err)).to.equal(null);
pm.expect(res.code).to.equal(200);
var FX = pm.variables.get('providerErrorFixtureUrl');
// wire: the requests that reached the fixture, bytes as they arrived.

function wire(cb) { pm.sendRequest({ url: FX + '/__wire', method: 'GET' }, function (err, res) { pm.test('the fixture answered /__wire', function () { pm.expect(err, String(err)).to.equal(null); pm.expect(res.code).to.equal(200); }); cb(res.json().data[0].calls); }); }
function imageCalls(calls) { return calls.filter(function (c) { return c.path === '/v1/images/generations' || c.path === '/v1/images/edits'; }); }

pm.test('the client gets 200 and a server-sent event stream', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.equal(200); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type'), JSON.stringify(pm.response.headers.toObject())).to.match(/^text\/event-stream/); });
var text = pm.response.text();
var events = text.split('\n').filter(function (l) { return l.indexOf('data: {') === 0; }).map(function (l) { return JSON.parse(l.slice(6)); });
